38: func Parse(filename string, input []byte) ([]ServerBlock, error) {
39: 	// unfortunately, we must copy the input because parsing must
40: 	// remain a read-only operation, but we have to expand environment
41: 	// variables before we parse, which changes the underlying array (#4422)

60: // It returns all the tokens from the input, unstructured
61: // and in order. It may mutate input as it expands env vars.

63: 	return Tokenize(replaceEnvVars(input), filename)

66: // replaceEnvVars replaces all occurrences of environment variables.
67: // It mutates the underlying array and returns the updated slice.
68: func replaceEnvVars(input []byte) []byte {
69: 	var offset int
70: 	for {
71: 		begin := bytes.Index(input[offset:], spanOpen)
72: 		if begin < 0 {
73: 			break
74: 		}
75: 		begin += offset // make beginning relative to input, not offset
76: 		end := bytes.Index(input[begin+len(spanOpen):], spanClose)
77: 		if end < 0 {
78: 			break
79: 		}
80: 		end += begin + len(spanOpen) // make end relative to input, not begin
81: 
82: 		// get the name; if there is no name, skip it
83: 		envString := input[begin+len(spanOpen) : end]
84: 		if len(envString) == 0 {
85: 			offset = end + len(spanClose)
86: 			continue
87: 		}
88: 
89: 		// split the string into a key and an optional default
90: 		envParts := strings.SplitN(string(envString), envVarDefaultDelimiter, 2)
91: 
92: 		// do a lookup for the env var, replace with the default if not found
93: 		envVarValue, found := os.LookupEnv(envParts[0])
94: 		if !found && len(envParts) == 2 {
95: 			envVarValue = envParts[1]
96: 		}
97: 
98: 		// get the value of the environment variable
99: 		// note that this causes one-level deep chaining
100: 		envVarBytes := []byte(envVarValue)
101: 
102: 		// splice in the value
103: 		input = append(input[:begin],
104: 			append(envVarBytes, input[end+len(spanClose):]...)...)

Issue body actions

There is a **BUG** in the way LeastConnSelection policy is selecting an upstream for the reverse proxy.  
The following is the code of the select method of LeastConnSelection struct which chooses the upstream:  
[caddy/blob/master/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/selectionpolicies.go](https://github.com/caddyserver/caddy/blob/master/modules/caddyhttp/reverseproxy/selectionpolicies.go)

```
// Select selects the up host with the least number of connections in the
// pool. If more than one host has the same least number of connections,
// one of the hosts is chosen at random.
func (LeastConnSelection) Select(pool UpstreamPool, _ *http.Request, _ http.ResponseWriter) *Upstream {
	var bestHost *Upstream
	var count int
	leastReqs := -1

	for _, host := range pool {
		if !host.Available() {
			continue
		}
		numReqs := host.NumRequests()
		if leastReqs == -1 || numReqs < leastReqs {
			leastReqs = numReqs
			count = 0
		}

		// among hosts with same least connections, perform a reservoir
		// sample: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Reservoir_sampling
		if numReqs == leastReqs {
			count++
			if count > 1 || (weakrand.Int()%count) == 0 { //nolint:gosec
				bestHost = host
			}
		}
	}

	return bestHost
}
```

This **always selects the last upstream which has the least number of active requests, but it should randomly choose among all the upstreams which have the least number of active requests**, reservoir sampling is implemented incorrecly, because of the extra condition (count>1) in the if clause.

part.text:
Fixed. Root cause: commit 9cde7155 (#5540) stopped rewriting `Token.File` for imported tokens, but `Dispenser.isNewLine()`/`isNextOnNewLine()` relied on imported tokens having a different file to detect line boundaries in the spliced token stream. Snippet tokens keep the same file and often *lower* line numbers than the surrounding tokens, so an `import` inside a `handle` block was no longer seen as starting a new line and was never expanded during parse-time — hence "unrecognized directive: import".

Changes (caddyconfig/caddyfile):
- `dispenser.go:457` — `isNewLine()` and `isNextOnNewLine()` now also treat tokens imported through different import chains (`Token.imports`) as being on different lines (an import always begins a new line).
- `parse.go:455` — `doImport()` now copies the `imports` slice before appending, so the shared backing array of tokens in `p.definedSnippets` is never mutated across multiple expansions of the same snippet.

Validation: the exact config from the issue now adapts correctly (`respond foobar 202` inside the `handle` route); verified site-level imports, double snippet expansion with different args, and the full `./caddyconfig/caddyfile` and `./caddyconfig/httpcaddyfile` test suites pass (`-count=1`), plus `go vet`/`go build` are clean.
